title: "Quiz: R calculations"
---

[Lecture](../lectures/06-r-basics/lec.qmd) · [Exercises](06-r-basics.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** What does the last line print?

```r
initial_mm <- 20
final_mm <- 37
growth_mm <- final_mm - initial_mm
final_mm <- 39
growth_mm
```

(i) 17  (ii) 19  (iii) 39

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Which assignment last changed `growth_mm`?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(i), 17. R stored that result when the subtraction ran. Running
`growth_mm <- final_mm - initial_mm` again would update it to 19.
:::

---

**Q2.** Three plants have initial lengths `c(20, 22, 19)` mm and final lengths
`c(37, 40, 34)` mm, in the same plant order. What are their growth values and
mean growth?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Subtract position by position, then divide the total growth by three.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Growth is `c(17, 18, 15)` mm. The mean is `50 / 3`, about 16.67 mm.
The matching plant order makes the position-by-position subtraction meaningful.
:::

---

**Q3.** Which survives closing a fresh R session: an object created only in the
Console, or instructions saved in `day06.R`? How can you recreate the object?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
One is in session memory; the other is a file on storage.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The saved script survives. Open it and run the instructions from the top to
recreate its objects. This assumes the session workspace was not separately saved
and restored.
:::

---

**Q4.** A collected product mass is 0.62 g and the supplied maximum is 1.00 g.
Using `yield_percent = 100 × collected mass / maximum mass`, what is the yield?
What would change if the collected mass were 0.70 g?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Both masses use grams, so their units cancel in the ratio.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The yields are 62% and 70%, respectively.
:::

---

**Q5.** Amount in mol is `mass_g / molar_mass_g_mol`. Concentration in mol/L is
amount divided by final solution volume in litres. For 0.2922 g, 58.44 g/mol,
and 100 mL final solution, what is the concentration in mmol/L?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Convert 100 mL to 0.100 L. Multiply mol/L by 1000 to obtain mmol/L.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Amount is `0.2922 / 58.44 = 0.005` mol. Concentration is
`0.005 / 0.100 = 0.050` mol/L, or **50 mmol/L**.
:::

---

**Q6.** In the previous question, what happens to concentration if you double
only the mass? What if you instead double only the final volume?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Mass is in the numerator; final volume is in the denominator.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Doubling mass gives 100 mmol/L. Restoring the original mass and doubling final
volume gives 25 mmol/L.
:::
